📦 Fine-tunes & Quantizations (community fine-tunes, GGUF, AWQ)

Model Author Likes Downloads Summary
unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF unsloth 4,388 7,118,363 Official Unsloth GGUF quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B; 7.1M downloads make it the go-to quantized bundle for local LLM inference via llama.cpp.
DavidAU/Qwen3.8-27B-TURBO-Fable-Cold-Fusion-735-882-Heretic-Uncensored-NEO-CODER-MAX-MTP-GGUF DavidAU 974 1,256,962 Heavily merged/uncensored fine-tune with MTP (multi-token prediction) quantized to GGUF; 1.2M downloads show appetite for opinionated, coding-optimized blends.
ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF ISTA-DASLab 1,438 1,154,265 GSQ (Group-wise Scalar Quantization) + RCO (Rotation-Consistent Optimization) mixed-precision GGUF; 1.15M downloads validate advanced quantization research impact.
prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf prism-ml 1,266 1,516,960 2-bit ternary quantization of Bonsai-2-27B via Hadamard transform; 1.5M downloads prove extreme compression (≈1.5 GB) retains usable quality for CPU inference.
ukisai/Swift-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF ukisai 320 120,740 GGUF quant of the Swift-Qwen3.8-27B efficient-thinking variant; targets users wanting both speed optimizations and quantization in one package.
dealignai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-UNCENSORED-FP8 dealignai 312 34,230 Uncensored fine-tune of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in FP8; 34K downloads reflect demand for alignment-removed multimodal models with efficient inference.
prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-mlx-2bit prism-ml 258 23,111 MLX-format 2-bit ternary quant for Apple Silicon; 23K downloads highlight growing MLX ecosystem for on-device LLM deployment.
ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF ISTA-DASLab 175 31,099 GSQ/RCO quantization applied to Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; extends mixed-precision research to the newer Flash architecture.

Ecosystem Signal

The Qwen 3.8 family (base, Flash-Next, and dozens of community quantizations/merges) has become the de facto open-weight hub—mirroring Llama-3.1’s position six months ago—while DeepSeek and Z.ai’s "Flash" lines cement a new efficiency tier for multimodal models. Open weights still dominate downloads, but the action is increasingly in derivatives: 8 of the top 30 are community GGUF/MLX quantizations or merges, and ISTA-DASLab’s GSQ/RCO mixed-precision work shows quantization research moving from "post-training compression" to "architecture-aware co-design." Video generation has crossed the adoption chasm (MiniMax-H3 4.3M, LTX-2.5 1.6M downloads), and the 254M downloads of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 remind us that embedding models remain the highest-volume, lowest-visibility layer of the stack. MoE architectures (Edge0, InternLM, XingChen) are proliferating in open weights, but active-param counts stay modest (3–4B), suggesting the community is still optimizing for single-GPU/CPU inference rather than scaling out.

Worth Exploring

  1. ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF — Best-in-class mixed-precision quantization (GSQ+RCO) on the current flagship multimodal model; 1.15M downloads and academic backing make it the reference for "how low can we go without quality collapse."
  2. Lightricks/LTX-2.5 — Single-file diffusion model covering text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video; 1.6M downloads and permissive license make it the practical starting point for any video generation product.
  3. Edge0/Edge0-35B-A3B-preview — Rare open MoE with 3B active params targeting edge inference; studying its expert routing and MLX integration offers a window into the next wave of sparse, on-device LLMs.

item.content:encoded:
Tech Community AI Digest 2026-09-20

Sources: Dev.to (30 articles) + Lobste.rs (9 stories) | Generated: 2026-09-20 04:36 UTC

Tech Community AI Digest — 2026-09-20

Today's Highlights

Developers are grappling with the double standard around AI usage in hiring — candidates rejected for using AI tools while interviewers use them freely. A strong practical thread runs through both communities: testing AI-generated code (1,558 green tests that never actually ran), agent permissions and security (MCP servers that change behavior post-approval), and token-efficient agentic workflows. The emergence of AGENTS.md (6.2% of active GitHub repos) and Jev/TypeSafe System One signals a shift toward structured, auditable agent decision-making. Security incidents — OpenAI's monorepo breach via libheif and models leaving hidden notes — remind us that supply-chain and alignment risks are very real.

Dev.to Highlights

Article Reactions Comments Summary
I got rejected for using AI in an interview. Then I watched the interviewer do it. 20 3 A candidate was rejected for using AI during a coding interview, only to discover the interviewer used AI to evaluate the submission. Highlights the hypocrisy and lack of clear policies around AI-assisted hiring.
What Do You Do While AI Codes? I Make Mine Argue With Itself. 17 3 Instead of passively watching AI generate code, the author sets up multiple LLM agents to debate and critique each other's output, catching hallucinations and design flaws before human review.
I Let AI Write My Tests for 6 Months. Here Is What Actually Survived Production 14 12 After six months of AI-generated Playwright tests, only tests with explicit human-specified assertions and realistic data survived; green tests often asserted nothing and masked missing auth checks.
AI Is Making You a Worse Engineer and a Better Employee 11 3 Argues that AI optimizes for output velocity (employee metrics) at the expense of deep understanding and craft (engineering metrics), creating a silent deskilling effect.
1,558 Tests Green and No Auth: The Tests That Never Actually Ran 7 0 A test suite showed 1,558 passing tests but zero authentication coverage — tests like test_all_adapters_importable asserted nothing and would pass even if every adapter was broken.
Token-Efficient Agentic Development — Part 1: What Are You Actually Paying For? 6 3 Breaks down the hidden costs of agentic workflows: context window churn, redundant tool calls, and verbose reasoning traces. Offers patterns for prompt compression and deterministic tool routing.
How common is AGENTS.md, really? I sampled GitHub: 6.2% of active repos, 1.0% of all repos 4 11 Empirical study of AGENTS.md adoption across GitHub: 6.2% of active repositories use it, revealing emerging conventions for agent instructions, tool allowlists, and memory policies.
AI Agent Permissions: Designing Secure Access for Autonomous AI 3 1 Proposes capability-based permission models for AI agents: isolated identities, policy engines, and deterministic enforcement boundaries to prevent privilege escalation.
OpenAI monorepo reached via libheif and SSO flaws 5 0 A $6,500 bounty writeup: chaining a libheif heap overflow in OpenAI's forum with an SSO identity flaw to access the internal monorepo. Supply-chain and auth flaws in AI infra.
The MCP server that changes its mind after you approve it 1 2 MCP tool descriptions are re-fetched on every connection without pinning; a server can behave correctly during review and change behavior afterward — a TOCTOU vulnerability in agent tooling.

Lobste.rs Highlights

Story Score Comments Summary
I Built Non-Autoregressive Decision Models a Year Ago. Then a Frontier Lab Called It a "Breakthrough" · discuss 44 4 An independent researcher built non-autoregressive decision models (System 1/2 architecture) a year before a major lab rebranded it as a breakthrough. Discussion on credit, open research, and the hype cycle.
A Letter from a Machine Learning Engineer · discuss 27 14 A reflective piece on the ML engineer's role shifting from model-building to prompt-engineering and eval pipelines. Captures the identity crisis and pragmatic adaptation in the field.
kicking the tires on jev (TypeSafe's System One model) with 2048 · discuss 15 2 Hands-on evaluation of Jev (TypeSafe's deterministic decision engine) using the game 2048. Shows Jev returning probabilities instead of prose, enabling formal verification of agent decisions.
Laya — 33ms Multilingual System 1 Decision Engine · discuss 5 3 Laya achieves 33ms latency for multilingual System 1 (fast, intuitive) decisions. Relevant for real-time agent routing and low-latency tool selection in production pipelines.
openarm: A fully open-source humanoid arm for physical AI research · discuss 4 0 Open-source humanoid arm hardware for embodied AI research. Contact-rich manipulation, open firmware, and sim-to-real tooling — lowering the barrier for physical AI experimentation.

Community Pulse

Both Dev.to and Lobste.rs are converging on pragmatic, production-grade concerns: developers have moved past "wow, AI codes" to "how do I test, secure, and audit what AI produces?" The AGENTS.md standard is gaining traction as a contract between humans and agents, while Jev/TypeSafe and Laya represent a push toward deterministic, verifiable decision engines (System 1) rather than opaque LLM reasoning. Security is a sharp thread — MCP TOCTOU flaws, OpenAI's monorepo breach, and models leaving hidden notes for successors all signal that AI supply-chain and alignment risks are no longer theoretical. Practitioners are building eval pipelines, guardrails for silent failures (200 OK but wrong), and human-in-the-loop patterns to catch degradation. The hiring double standard reflects a broader cultural lag: organizations want AI velocity but lack policies for attribution, liability, and skill preservation.

Worth Reading

  1. I Let AI Write My Tests for 6 Months. Here Is What Actually Survived Production — The most concrete, battle-tested account of AI-generated test quality; the comment thread (12 comments) adds real-world validation patterns.
  2. A Letter from a Machine Learning Engineer (Lobste.rs, 27 pts, 14 comments) — A rare, honest reflection on the role shift from modeling to prompting/evals; the discussion surfaces career strategy and tooling gaps.
  3. The MCP server that changes its mind after you approve it — A critical TOCTOU vulnerability in the emerging MCP standard; essential reading for anyone building agent tooling or reviewing MCP servers.

Macro Market Dashboard 2026-09-20

Sources: FRED + FINRA | 16 indicators | Generated: 2026-09-20 04:36 UTC

⚠️ Informational only, not financial advice.

1. Macro Snapshot

The Fed has resumed tightening with a 25 bp hike to 3.88 %, while the balance sheet remains stable near $6.75 T. Long‑term yields are highly restrictive at 4.94 % and the yield curve is barely positive (0.25 %), signaling tight financial conditions. Credit spreads are calm at 2.70 % and the VIX at 15.44 reflects complacency. However, oil above $100/bbl and PPI at +5.4 % YoY keep upstream inflation pressure elevated, while core CPI (+2.8 %) and core PCE (+3.3 %) remain well above the 2 % target. The labor market is tight (claims 196k, unemployment 4.1 %) but consumer sentiment is deeply weak (55.2). Retail leverage is expanding (+2.6 % MoM). 3. Money Market & Bond Watch

The provided NSO excerpts cover CPI, gold/USD price indices, public investment disbursement, FDI registration/disbursement, and trade data. 4. Regime Read

Vietnam’s equity regime is caught between strong domestic fundamentals and tightening external financial conditions. On the domestic side, 8M26 GDP‑tracking data are robust: disbursed FDI (+12% YoY) and registered FDI (+55% YoY) signal sustained industrial investment, public capital spending is accelerating (50.5% of plan vs 45.3% a year ago), and export growth (+22.4% YoY) remains FDI‑driven. However, the trade deficit has swung to $20.5bn (from a $14bn surplus), imports are surging +35%, and August CPI (4.89% YoY) breaches the 4.5% ceiling, leaving the SBV little scope to cut rates. Externally, the DXY has risen 1.33% in 20 days and US 10Y yields have climbed 6.24% to 4.94%, widening the yield differential and pressuring the dong — though the spot rate has barely moved (YTD -0.69%), implying active SBV management. The VN30F1M basis is slightly positive, and the VNM ETF is up 2.8% over 20 days, but without domestic foreign net‑flow or turnover data the liquidity picture is incomplete. Regime call: Late‑cycle expansion with external vulnerability — equities supported by earnings momentum but capped by FX/yield constraints; expect range‑bound trade with a downside bias if US yields break higher.

item.content:encoded:
Vietnam Interest Rate Macro Dashboard 2026-09-20

Sources: SBV + FRED + Vietcombank | Interbank session: 2026-09-15 | 50 sessions retrieved | Generated: 2026-09-20 04:36 UTC

⚠️ Informational only, not financial advice.

Vietnam Interest Rate Macro Dashboard

As of 2026-09-20 (interbank data from 2026-09-15 session)

1. Executive Summary

The SBV has kept policy rates unchanged for 1,282 days (since 2023-03-18), maintaining a neutral policy stance. Interbank rates trade well below the refinancing corridor ceiling (overnight 3.69% vs 4.50%; 1-week 4.20% vs 4.50%), signalling highly liquid domestic conditions. The single most important tension is the negative VND-USD overnight spread (-0.19pp), which binds the SBV’s ability to ease further despite ample local liquidity.

2. Policy Rate Table

Policy rate Level Effective from Standing for Role
Refinancing rate (lãi suất tái cấp vốn) 4.500% 2023-03-18 Ceiling Corridor ceiling
Discount rate (lãi suất tái chiết khấu) 3.000% 2023-03-18 Floor Corridor floor

3. Interbank Table

Tenor Rate 1 session 20 sessions 30 sessions Turnover (bn VND) Turnover 1s Reading
Overnight 3.69% -0.68pp -2.08pp -2.53pp 930,118 +0.6% Sharp drop, ample liquidity
1 Week 4.20% -0.43pp -1.51pp -2.26pp 8,595 +57.9% Moderate decline, high turnover growth
2 Week 4.67% -0.49pp -1.46pp -2.17pp 2,500 -50.0% Declining, turnover halved
1 Month 5.65% +0.06pp -1.31pp -1.55pp 7,619 +74.0% Slight rise, strong turnover growth
3 Month 6.89% +0.04pp -0.63pp -0.65pp 2,277 -2.1% Flat, turnover stable
6 Month 7.47% -1.00pp +0.42pp -0.09pp 1,006 +112.2% Sharp drop, turnover surged
9 Month 8.12% 0.00pp -1.14pp -1.14pp 512 0.0% Unchanged, low turnover

4. Policy vs Reality Gap

The refinancing rate (4.50%) sits 0.81pp above the overnight rate (3.69%) and 0.30pp above the 1-week rate (4.20%). Both interbank tenors trade below the policy ceiling, confirming excessive liquidity — money is cheap and sitting idle in the banking system. Turnover is heavily concentrated in the shortest tenors: overnight + 1-week account for 98.5% of total volume (952,627 bn VND). Because this concentration occurs at low rates (not elevated), it reflects the market’s natural trading hub rather than a funding crunch. The system is awash with reserves, and the SBV’s corridor floor (3.00%) remains the effective anchor for the shortest money.

5. External & Structural Filter

VND-USD spread: The VND overnight rate (3.69%) runs 0.19pp below the effective fed funds rate (3.88%), a negative carry that makes holding VND unattractive for carry trades. This spread is the binding constraint on further SBV easing; even with abundant domestic liquidity, the central bank cannot push short rates materially lower without triggering capital outflow pressure. The USD/VND spot sell rate has fallen 0.27% over the past month (VND stronger), offering a temporary buffer but not reversing the structural spread disadvantage.

OMO / T-bill activity: ❔ insufficient data — no source for SBV open-market operations or Treasury bill issuance is provided. The observed rate path (steady decline across most tenors over 20–30 sessions) would be consistent with net liquidity injection, but no operation can be asserted.

Credit-growth quota: ❔ insufficient data — no quota figure or utilisation rate is available. Seasonality: mid-September is not a quarter-end, but corporate tax payments in the third month of the quarter can create transient liquidity drains; the recent volatility (overnight swinging 1.19% → 6.01% → 3.69% over three weeks) is compatible with such flows.

6. Transmission & Sentiment

Effectiveness score: The 1-week rate trades 0.30pp below the refinancing rate, inside the ±0.5pp neutral band. The market is following the SBV’s lead — policy transmission is functional, not blocked by friction.

Curve shape: The 3-month/overnight slope is +3.20pp (6.89% vs 3.69%), a normal upward slope pricing steady-to-higher rates ahead. No inversion signals an imminent crunch.

Trend: Over the last 10 published sessions (2026-08-26 → 2026-09-15) the overnight rate has been highly volatile (range 1.19%–6.01%) but has fallen sharply in the most recent three sessions (5.16% → 4.37% → 3.69%). The 1-week rate mirrors this pattern. The short end is currently falling, but the trend is noisy and not yet established as a steady downtrend.

7. Macro Market Impact

Channel Direction Mechanism
Equities (VN-Index) Supportive Falling short-end rates lower the domestic risk-free rate; USD/VND stable (-0.27% over 1m) removes currency headwind — precondition for equity re-rating.
Exchange rate Pressuring Negative VND-USD overnight spread (-0.19pp) is the classic setup for VND depreciation pressure; recent spot strength is a cyclical counter-trend, not a structural fix.
Banking system (NIM & deposit rates) Neutral Interbank funding (3.69–4.20%) trades below typical deposit rates (~4.5–5.5%), so NIM not squeezed; ample liquidity removes urgency to cut deposit rates further.
Real estate Supportive Lower short-term funding costs reduce developer carry costs and mortgage rate ceilings; stable currency limits imported input-cost inflation.
Household deposits Neutral Banks face no funding stress (interbank below policy), so deposit-rate cuts can pause; households see no immediate pass-through to lower yields.

8. Outlook & Risks

Over the next 1–3 months, the overnight rate is likely to remain anchored near 3.5–4.0%, pinned by the SBV’s corridor floor (3.00%) and the negative VND-USD spread that prevents the central bank from cutting policy rates. The primary risk is a Fed easing cycle — if the FOMC cuts before the SBV, the spread could widen further, forcing SBV tightening to defend the VND. Conversely, a Fed hold or hike would deepen the negative carry, increasing capital-outflow risk. Quarter-end seasonality (late September/early October) may trigger a transient liquidity drain as corporates pay taxes, briefly lifting overnight rates. Inflation data (not in this pipeline) remains the swing factor: a surprise uptick would force SBV tightening regardless of the spread, while a downside print would give cover for a policy-rate cut — but only if the VND-USD spread permits.
